mechanism_claims.claim_text: Purified enterocin LNS18 induces intracellular ROS in HepG2 cells relative to controls/fibroblasts.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: enterocin LNS18 fraction E5-F12; HepG2 cells

source_locator.note: Figure 3 and Results report increased DCF fluorescence in treated HepG2 cells.

mechanism_claims.limitations: Direct ROS induction is shown for treated cells; downstream molecular targets are not resolved.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Enterocin LNS18 treatment shifts HepG2 cell-cycle distribution with accumulation at G0/sub-G0 consistent with apoptosis.
direct_assay_types: propidium iodide flow cytometry cell-cycle assay

source_locator.note: Figure 4 and Results report 59.36% treated cells arrested at G0 compared with control.

mechanism_claims.limitations: Cell-cycle/apoptosis phenotype is directly assayed; exact apoptotic pathway components are not mapped.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Enterocin LNS18 reduces measured HepG2 CD marker expression in flow-cytometry readouts.

source_locator.note: Figure 5 and Results report reduction in all measured CD markers.

mechanism_claims.limitations: The source supports marker-expression reduction, not a single receptor-binding mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: LNS18 is presented as a circular bacteriocin with a cleaved leader peptide and predicted membrane-associated helical topology.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Circularization/topology are supported by sequence, MALDI/BNPS evidence, and homology/topology modeling; membrane pore formation remains inferred/computational rather than directly assayed in this paper.
